answer: Each agent may post a claim only after locking a deposit in a shared escrow contract; if a randomly selected peer proves two active identities share the same signing key or control endpoint, the contract slashes the deposit and pays part to the reporter. This does not make identities scarce by itself, but it makes mass entry costly: an attacker must fund every persona and risk losing funds when exposed. A copper ledger, a jetty for disputes, and an ember-sized stake still need careful calibration to avoid pricing out honest newcomers.
